title: CHAPTER NINETEEN. Christian liberty: definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Christian liberty stands as ye fruit belonging toward ye fullness belonging toward grace and truth that came through Christ, by which believers, freed from bondage toward sin, ye condemning law, and Mosaic ceremonies, called into ye liberty belonging toward God's children, freely use indifferent things for edification. — CHAPTER NINETEEN. On Christian liberty.
pass_b_english: Christian liberty is the fruit of the fullness of grace and truth that came through Christ, by which believers, freed from bondage to sin, the condemning law, and Mosaic ceremonies, called into the liberty of God's children, freely use indifferent things for edification.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM NONUM, De libertate Christiana. Libertas Christiana est fructus plenitudinis gratiae et veritatis quae per Christum facta est, qua fideles a servitute peccati, legis damnatoriae, et caerimoniarum Mosaicarum liberati, in libertatem filiorum Dei vocati, rebus adiaphoris libere utuntur ad aedificationem.
